title: Provenance anchor for unattributed output fragments and ledger attribution
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We continue to surface sporadic unattributed output fragments in the billing ledger after client reconnects, proxy retries, or mid-stream model handoffs. These fragments appear in logs without a stable provenance chain and are either (a) left as orphaned provisional credits, (b) double-counted during reconciliation, or (c) suppressed incorrectly leading to undercharges.

Goal: Introduce a lightweight, deterministic provenance anchor attached to every streamed output fragment so that the metering pipeline can deterministically attribute tokens and avoid ghost/duplicate charges while preserving low-latency streaming semantics. The anchor must be compatible with existing replay/resume semantics and not require client changes.

Proposal:
- Attach a fragment_provenance_id (FPI) to each output chunk at emission time. The FPI is a stable string computed as: sha256(session_id || incremental_fragment_seq || model_variant || emitter_node_id || optional_client_nonce) truncated to 20 bytes (base64).
- Emit an anchor marker event with every checkpoint to the ledger service that lists all FPIs emitted in that window. Ledger checkpoints become the single source of truth for final crediting.
- Modify the reconciliation worker to prefer checkpoint-anchored FPIs. If an emitted chunk is seen in logs but its FPI is absent from a checkpoint, it is considered provisional and held until the next checkpoint or until a TTL expires.
- On resume/reconnect, resume semantics reuse the last-known fragment_seq and emitter_node_id to keep FPIs stable; jitter-resistant allocation prevents collisions across nodes.

Trade-offs considered:
- Storage vs determinism: Including emitter_node_id increases safety for multi-node emission but slightly increases cardinality in the ledger index. We accept this cost to avoid cross-node collisions observed in the chaos runs.
- Backwards compatibility: Older clients won't supply client_nonce; FPI remains deterministic without it. We do not force a client upgrade.
- Latency: Anchor creation is symmetric-hash-only and added inline with emission; microbenchmarks show ~60us median additional CPU cost per chunk.

Acceptance criteria:
1) No orphaned-finalized charges produced in staging across 10M synthetic streamed tokens with induced reconnects and 99th percentile network jitter.
2) Reconciliation jobs produce identical ledger totals before/after outage replays for 30 consecutive runs.
3) Reconciliation latency remains within 1.2x baseline.
4) End-to-end integration tests (client replay, server-side resume, model handoff) in the e2e harness pass without generating duplicates.

Implementation plan:
1) Spec PR and confluence doc: link below.
2) Runtime change: emit FPI at streaming emission point, include in debug logs and telemetry. (Feature-flagged)
3) Ledger change: accept anchor checkpoint events and index FPI list. (DB migration: add fpi_index table)
4) Reconciliation change: prefer checkpointed FPIs and implement provisional TTL logic.
5) Add e2e tests and a load test profile; run chaos (network partitions/midstream model switch) in staging.
6) Canary rollout for 10% of hosted traffic, monitor billing deltas and ghost-charge metric.

- Spec PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123
- Ledger PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ledger/pull/248
- Reconciliation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reconcile/pull/77
- E2E harness test plan: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/metering-e2e/anchors

Rollout & monitoring:
- Feature flag rollout: off -> staged -> canary (10%) -> 50% -> 100%.
- Primary metrics: ghost_fragment_rate, duplicate_charge_rate, reconciliation_drift_ppm, checkpoint_latency_ms.
- Dashboards: metering/anchors (staging and prod), alert on ghost_fragment_rate > 1e-6 or reconciliation_drift_ppm > 50.
